title: Universal Law Discovery Engine - Technology Profile
description: Public edition: AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.
body:
Universal Law Discovery Engine. AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 1 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Reality Engineering and Universal Physics". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Sparse-identification methods have recovered governing equations from real experimental datasets, so the core capability is demonstrated on narrow problems; a fully general discovery engine remains research-grade.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Universal Law Discovery Engine - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.
body:
Known science foundations of Universal Law Discovery Engine.

Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy, Brunton, Proctor and Kutz, 2016) recovered fluid-flow and oscillator equations from measurements. Symbolic regression systems such as Eureqa and AI Feynman (Udrescu and Tegmark, 2020) rediscover textbook physical laws from data. Active research extends these methods to noisy, high-dimensional experimental systems with partial observation.

Key quantity check (SINDy term recovery on benchmark systems: recovered terms / candidate terms): computed ratio 1 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.05. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Universal Law Discovery Engine - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Universal Law Discovery Engine.

Measurement noise and incomplete state observation limit which equations are identifiable from data. The space of candidate terms grows combinatorially with system dimension. Discovered equations require independent experimental validation before they count as laws.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 14 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is compute per run vs candidate law evaluation time at 14 orders of magnitude (compute per run larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Universal Law Discovery Engine - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.
body:
Unresolved problems for Universal Law Discovery Engine, in priority order (research burden index 19, 1 blocking):

Scaling to noisy real-world sensor data (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Unifying discovered laws across domains (severity 2/3, tractability 1/3; priority 6).

Guarantees of identifiability (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

description: Public edition: AI that derives candidate physical laws from experimental data and searches for simpler unifying principles.
body:
What would count as evidence of success for Universal Law Discovery Engine:

Recovers known laws from synthetic noisy data (weight 0.3; SATISFIED).

Discovers a previously unknown relation confirmed experimentally (weight 0.5; not yet satisfied).

Matches human experts on law-discovery benchmarks (weight 0.2; SATISFIED).

Evidence confidence: 0.5 (2 of 3 criteria satisfied). Verdict: partial. Confidence here measures satisfied evidence, not belief.
